advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Add cases asserting the exact truncated bullet length (240 chars ending in `…`) and that a detail of exactly 240 chars is emitted verbatim without an ellipsis.
evidence: adapter.py:123 `detail = f"{full_detail[:239]}…" if len(full_detail) > 240 else full_detail`
test only asserts `assert "…" in bullets[0]` (test_review_bot.py:258) — does not check truncated length or non-truncation of a boundary-length (≤240) detail
test_review_bot.py:242 `assert len(long_detail) > 240` — both parametrized cases use only very-long details; search for `239`/`240` in tests/unit found no boundary-length case
advisory.finding: The new test asserts only `"…" in bullets[0]` for the truncation behavior and drives both cases with details far exceeding 240 chars, so the length-gated truncation boundary is untested: the `len(full_detail) > 240` guard (a detail of exactly 240 chars must NOT be truncated) and the exact truncated length (`full_detail[:239]` + `…` = 240 chars) are never asserted. An off-by-one regression (`>=` vs `>`, or a wrong slice bound like `[:240]`) would still leave a `…` present and pass the test.
scenarios: An edit changing the guard to `>= 240` or the slice to `[:240]` (off-by-one) would produce a 241-char bullet or truncate a 240-char detail, yet the test still passes because `…` appears.
A detail exactly 240 chars long — should be emitted verbatim without ellipsis — is never exercised.
advisory.suggested_fix: Add parametrized/boundary cases: a 240-char detail asserts the bullet contains the full text and no `…`; a 241-char detail asserts the emitted detail equals `full_detail[:239] + '…'` and is exactly 240 chars long.
